## Approach

Since the donors are unaffected by the disaster, I built a synthetic‑control‑style predictor from the donor pool:

1. **Common signal:** The 29 donors share a strong common component (they all dip together at periods 6, 23, 36 and peak at 10, 29, 46, 55, 57). I computed the donor‑pool average **A(t)** for every period (1–60).
2. **Link the target to the pool:** Regressing the target on A(t) over the pre‑disaster periods 1–40 gives

 **target(t) ≈ –0.05 + 1.27 · A(t)**  (R² ≈ 0.46, residual sd ≈ 1.45)

 The slope > 1 means the target's vegetation swings about 27% more than a typical donor around the shared regional signal; the residual (sd ≈ 1.45) is site‑specific noise, which is the practical limit of forecast accuracy (≈ ±1.5 per period).
3. **Counterfactual:** Apply this fitted rule to the donor averages of periods 41–60 (the donors remain undisrupted there).

| Period | Donor avg | Counterfactual | | Period | Donor avg | Counterfactual |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 41 | 0.72 | 0.86 | | 51 | –1.19 | –1.56 |
| 42 | 0.27 | 0.30 | | 52 | 0.26 | 0.27 |
| 43 | 0.40 | 0.46 | | 53 | –0.91 | –1.21 |
| 44 | –1.31 | –1.71 | | 54 | –0.32 | –0.46 |
| 45 | –1.17 | –1.54 | | 55 | 1.32 | 1.62 |
| 46 | 1.19 | 1.47 | | 56 | –0.12 | –0.20 |
| 47 | –1.41 | –1.85 | | 57 | 2.16 | 2.70 |
| 48 | 1.43 | 1.77 | | 58 | 0.01 | –0.04 |
| 49 | –0.98 | –1.30 | | 59 | –1.15 | –1.52 |
| 50 | 0.28 | 0.31 | | 60 | –0.25 | –0.37 |

**Interpretation:** Without the disaster, the target would have continued oscillating around roughly its normal level (mean ≈ 0), with a strong regional high around period 57 (≈ 2.7) and lows around periods 44–47 and 51 (≈ –1.5 to –1.9). Once the actual post‑41 observations of the target are available, the disaster impact at each period is simply (actual value) − (counterfactual value above); a persistent negative gap would indicate lasting vegetation damage.
